data.title: CPTPP to start talks on accession of UAE, Indonesia, Philippines
data.description:
Members of the CPTPP Pacific Rim trade bloc have agreed to start accession negotiations with the United Arab Emirates, Indonesia and the Philippines, Vietnam's deputy trade minister said on Friday.

  • Members of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership also agreed during a meeting in Hanoi to advance negotiations to upgrade the agreement, Luong Hoang Thai said, according to remarks shared by his office

  • Focus areas for an upgrade include services trade, e-commerce, customs and trade facilitation, cross-border services and business competitiveness, Thai said

  • The CPTPP is the successor to the Trans-Pacific Partnership, a bloc originally led by the United States that was widely seen as a counterweight to China's influence before US President Donald Trump withdrew Washington from the pact in 2017

  • It now comprises Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Peru, Singapore, Vietnam and Britain

  • Deputy minister Thai said the CPTPP was confident in "reinforcing its leading role in promoting an open, stable, predictable and rules-based international trade and investment environment"

  • Its members also reaffirmed a determination to bring accession negotiations with Uruguay to an early conclusion

  • The scheduled two-day meeting took place hours after the Trump administration proposed tariffs on 14 of its trading partners – which included CPTPP members Japan, Malaysia, Singapore and Vietnam – following its investigation into excess factory capacity

data.title: UBS Cites Experts that Rising Social Security Costs Pressure Intermediaries; Shenzhen Rent Uptick Supports Home Prices
data.description:
UBS recently held an expert call with senior management of a leading Shenzhen real estate intermediary and competitor of KE Holdings Inc . Experts believed rising social security contributions are having a negative cost impact on intermediaries. Some Shenzhen agencies are reportedly exploring replacing traditional employment contracts with freelance agent models to reduce the social security costs borne by intermediary firms.

For KE Holdings, experts foresaw Lianjia stores may need to absorb additional costs, while third-party store owners may bear higher costs and close less profitable outlets, or adopt freelance agent models similar to other intermediaries.

UBS cited expert estimates that overall residential rents in Shenzhen will rebound by about 3%, with rents in core and non-core areas rising about 3.5% and 2.5% respectively. The new Huanggang Port was expected to have a exceptionally positive impact on nearby properties, with residential rents hiking about 10% and home prices increasing a milder 2.5%.

Experts considered rising rents provide fundamental support for Shenzhen home prices to stabilize, as more investors focus on properties where monthly rental income can cover mortgage payments. UBS maintained its Buy rating and USD26.6 TP on KE Holdings.

data.title: Toyota Motor Worldwide Production, Sales Drop In October
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - Japanese auto major Toyota Motor Corp. (TM, TYT.L, 7203.T) reported Friday that total group production and group sales for the month of October declined from last year.

Total group production was 953,989 vehicles in October, down 9.4 percent on a year before. Production inside Japan dropped 7.8 percent, and production outside Japan declined 10.5 percent.

Total group sales were 940,809 vehicles, down 6.3 percent. Sales inside Japan dropped 10.9 percent, and sales outside Japan fell 5.1 percent.

The drop in October production marks the fourth straight month of annual decline, while sales mark 9 straight months of decline.

For the year-to-date period, total production was 9.166 million vehicles, down 2.6 percent from last year, and total sales were 8.998 million vehicles, down 3.9 percent year-over-year.

In the overnight activity on the NYSE, Toyota shares were trading 1.39 percent lower at $212.80.

In Tokyo, the shares closed Friday's trading at 3,384.00 yen, up 0.21 percent.

data.title: Trump admin urged Venezuela, Iraq to quit OPEC, blocked Venezuela’s membership dues: Reuters
data.description:
The Trump administration encouraged Venezuela and Iraq to consider leaving OPEC earlier this year and prevented Venezuela from paying its annual membership dues to the group, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The moves targeted two of OPEC's five founding members, marking an unusually direct challenge to an organization President Donald Trump has long accused of keeping oil prices artificially high.

US officials were pushing for greater oil production and investment in both countries at the time, and some worried OPEC production limits could eventually constrain those ambitions, the report said.

The US pressure on Venezuela went far enough that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman intervened this summer, persuading the Trump administration not to press the issue further, people familiar with the matter said.

In Iraq, Prime Minister ‌Ali Faleh al-Zaidi raised the possibility of leaving OPEC at a government meeting this summer after discussions with US officials who encouraged the idea, the report added.

The US State Department did not answer questions about whether it had prevented Venezuela from paying its OPEC membership fee. But it ​confirmed Washington has the power to decide on Venezuela’s use of state funds, now held in a US-controlled account set up after Maduro's removal, the report said.

"The Department receives disbursement requests from the interim Venezuelan government and reviews the requests, including against a list of approved and prohibited uses of ​the foreign Government Deposit Funds," a State Department official told Reuters.

The official said that it was possible that lower-level US officials had raised the question of leaving OPEC with Venezuela's government earlier this year, but that "it has ⁠not been among the issues raised by high-level officials."

The State Department's conversations with Iraq, meanwhile, "have focused on improving energy infrastructure to increase production and transportation of energy, not OPEC," the official told the new agency.
